5.evidence_source: Participants completed the 10-item BAS-2 (Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015b; see Table 1).
5._section_summary: This Measures section (Study X) describes the instruments used: Body Appreciation was measured with the 10-item BAS-2; actual–ideal weight discrepancy (women only) was measured using the Photographic Figure Rating Scale (PFRS); self-esteem was measured with a 9-item Chinese-adapted Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (Cronbach's α = .86 in women and .88 in men); and life satisfaction was measured with the 5-item SWLS (Cronbach's α = .84 in women and .85 in men). Men did not complete the PFRS because no male version is available. The section does not report sample size, country, ages, BMI, education levels, survey method, or correlations between body appreciation and BMI.

6.evidence_source: Once ethics approval was obtained, we translated the five new items of the BAS-2 into Cantonese using the standard backtranslation technique.
6._section_summary: This Procedure section describes translation of five new BAS-2 items into Cantonese and participant recruitment between November 2014 and April 2015. Recruitment occurred in classroom settings where participants provided consent and completed anonymous questionnaires individually; no separate study numbers (e.g., 'Study 1') or multiple sample subsets are mentioned.

7.evidence_source: The text states: 'we also conducted one-sample t-tests to compare scores between our participants and the community sample means reported in Tylka and Wood-Barcalow's (2015b) Study 3, which used the same wording of the BAS-2 as in the present study.'
7._section_summary: This 'Statistical Analyses' section (unnamed study) describes the analytic procedures: sex-specific EFAs on the BAS-2, independent-samples and one-sample t-tests (including comparisons to Tylka & Wood-Barcalow's Study 3 community means), and bivariate correlations examining body appreciation with BMI, self-esteem, life satisfaction, age, and (for women) weight discrepancy; curvilinear relations with BMI were also considered for men. The section does not report sample size, demographic details (country, percent white, mean age, education), BMI measurement method, or numeric correlation coefficients.

8.evidence_source: The Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin (KMO) measure of sampling adequacy, KMO = .92, indicated that the BAS-2 items had adequate common variance for EFA.
8._section_summary: This 'Female Sample' section reports an exploratory factor analysis of BAS-2 items: Bartlett's test of sphericity was significant and KMO = .92, with EFA suggesting one dominant factor explaining 48.8% of item variance. The section notes item loadings ≥ .45 and parallel analysis supporting a single factor. No sample size, demographic information, BMI data, survey method, or correlations with BMI are reported, and no study numbering (e.g., 'Study 1') is provided.

9.evidence_source: Internal consistency coefficients of the BAS-2 items were very good for women (α = .90) and men (α = .91).
9._section_summary: This section reports between-group comparisons from the present study, noting very good internal consistency for BAS-2 and small sex differences (men > women) in body appreciation. It also compares the present sample to the community sample from Tylka and Wood-Barcalow (2015b, Study 3), finding that both women and men in the present study had higher body appreciation than their counterparts in Study 3.

10.evidence_source: Our results showed that the Chinese BAS-2 consists of a single factor in both women and men.
